# Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading

## Problem statement

The target-aware config (hangar) screen marks **every** weapon row with its
matchup against the chosen hex's boss — green `▲ EFFECTIVE` when the boss is
weak to it, red `▼ RESISTED` when the boss resists it — but it does so even for
rows the player **cannot act on**: weapons they cannot buy (short of salvage,
`NEED 40 min`, or still ring-gated, `RING 2`) and owned weapons whose pricey
upgrade they cannot afford. Highlighting a recommendation the player cannot act
on reads as "buy this", so the intel lies about what is available right now.

## Users

- **The new player with no salvage** — "I have 0 minerals; every weapon row is
  lit up as if I could bring or upgrade it. Only light up what I can act on."
- **The ring-1 player** — "A ring-2 weapon is shown in bright red as if my
  loadout choice matters; I cannot buy it yet."
- **The accessibility-minded player** — "The matchup must still be readable
  without colour wherever it is shown." (Repo CVD policy: never colour-only.)
- **The producer/maintainer** — "One shared model decides the highlight, so the
  game and `GymHangar` cannot drift and no scene owns a second rule."

Example user stories:

- As a player with no salvage, I still read the boss's intel and the `▲`/`▼`
  verdicts, but only the rows I could actually buy or upgrade are highlighted.
- As a player with enough salvage for one weapon, that row is highlighted and
  the ones I cannot afford render as ordinary disabled rows.
- As a player equipping a weapon I already own, the `LOADOUT` column keeps its
  full matchup highlight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Rows with no available action are not highlighted.** In the hangar screen's
  unlock tree, a `weapon` row the player cannot act on right now — purchase
  states `unaffordable` (`NEED … min`) and `gated` (`RING n`), and upgrade
  states `upgrade-unaffordable` and `capped` (`MAX`) — renders with **no**
  strong/weak colour and **no** strong/weak background tint, keeping the
  ordinary row styling (muted colour, its price/shortfall or `MAX` intact).
- **Rows with an available action keep their highlight.** A `weapon` row whose
  own action is available — a `buyable` purchase row and an `upgradable` upgrade
  row — keeps exactly today's behaviour: `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` marker,
  strong/weak colour and tint.
- **The `LOADOUT` column is unchanged.** Every starting-weapon row in the
  deployment selector (owned weapons, always toggleable) keeps its marker,
  colour and tint, because equipping/unequipping it is always available.
- **The marker stays on every weapon row.** The `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED`
  text tag is appended wherever the weapon has a strong/weak verdict, including
  the non-highlighted rows, so the intel stays readable without colour (CVD
  policy) and only the colour/tint follows affordability.
- **The shared model decides, and the gym agrees.** Whether a row is highlighted
  is published by `buildHangarScreenModel`/`buildHangarUnlockRows` (data beside
  the existing `matchup` verdict), never derived from the render-time
  interactive/actionable flag, so the read-only `GymHangar` render shows exactly
  the game's highlight; a test asserts the model, the game render and the gym
  render agree for the same payload.
- **Automated tests cover the matrix.** Model-level and render-level tests for
  `buyable` + strong/weak, `unaffordable` + strong/weak, `gated` + strong/weak,
  `upgradable` + strong/weak, `upgrade-unaffordable` + strong/weak, `capped` +
  strong/weak, and a `LOADOUT` row of each strength; plus a test that a
  non-highlighted row keeps its marker, price and shortfall.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, GDD §8.2, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A player choosing a loadout only sees the boss-counter highlight on weapon rows
they can actually act on right now, while the `▲`/`▼` intel stays readable
everywhere — so the green/red marks are a promise the player can keep.

## Assumptions (documented; producer may override at review)

- **A1 — "Cannot buy" = `unaffordable` or `gated`.** Both mean the purchase
  cannot happen now (`canBuy` returns `unaffordable` for a salvage shortfall and
  `gated` for a not-yet-reached ring), so neither row is highlighted.
  (Producer Q2 = (a).)
- **A2 — Marker retained, colour suppressed.** A non-highlighted row keeps the
  `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` text marker and only loses the colour and backing
  tint, so it reads as a normal row whose matchup is still legible without
  colour. (Producer Q1 = (a).)
- **A3 — LOADOUT yes, upgrade tree no.** The `LOADOUT` equipped/unequipped column
  keeps its highlight for owned weapons (the action is always available); in the
  main upgrade/purchase tree the highlight follows the row's **own** action, so
  an owned weapon whose upgrade is `upgrade-unaffordable` (or `capped`) is **not**
  highlighted, while an `upgradable` one is. (Producer Q3: "equipped/unequipped
  column yes, main selection for upgrade no".)
- **A3.1 — `capped` (`MAX`) counts as "no available action".** A maxed row has
  nothing left to buy, so it is not highlighted; the player still sees the
  weapon highlighted in the `LOADOUT` column. Recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in
  case the producer would rather a maxed weapon keep its highlight.
- **A4 — Display only.** Prices, ring gating, ownership, the matchup resolver
  (`src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`) and the `TARGET INTEL` block are
  unchanged; this item changes only which rows are highlighted (parent
  AH-0MWMRWCY2001HWGR assumption A7 stands — the mechanical matchup is
  AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ).
- **A5 — No new persistence.** No payload schema or store change.
- **A6 — Existing fixtures must be re-baselined.** Today's matchup tests use a
  0-salvage payload whose weapons are all **owned**, so those rows are
  `upgrade-unaffordable` and (per A3) lose their colour: the rendered-colour
  assertion for `buy:spread` in `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` must change, and
  a fixture with salvage must be added to keep a positive highlight assertion.
  The `matchup` verdict and the `▲`/`▼` labels survive unchanged.

## Constraints

- **Model, not render, decides the highlight.** `renderHangarScreen` reports
  every row non-actionable in a read-only render (the gym), so keying the
  highlight off `actionable` would silently blank every mark in `GymHangar` and
  break gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **One shared code path.** No second matchup/highlight rule in `HangarScene`,
  `GymHangar` or the map; the pure model plus the one renderer stay the only
  place the rule lives.
- **Never colour-only.** The glyph tag stays on every weapon row with a verdict;
  a suppressed row must remain an ordinary readable row (price + shortfall, or
  `MAX`), not an unexplained blank.
- **No layout change.** No new rows or sections; `hangarLowestRowY` /
  bottom-row geometry are untouched.
- **No economy change.** The affordability verdicts are the economy's own
  (`canBuy`, `costToUpgrade`); this item only reads them.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Auto-buying the counter weapon, hiding non-weapon rows,
  dimming the `TARGET INTEL` block, or changing prices/gating are out of scope —
  record them as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Risks

- **Gym-parity regression (high).** Deriving the highlight from render-time
  `actionable` would blank every mark in the read-only gym; mitigated by
  publishing the decision in the model and asserting it in `GymHangar.test.ts`.
- **Test re-baseline churn (medium, expected).** Two existing tests assert a
  colour on rows that are now non-highlighted (0-salvage owned weapons); they
  must be updated deliberately, with a salvage-bearing fixture keeping the
  positive case covered.
- **Player surprise on `MAX` rows (low).** A maxed weapon loses its tree
  highlight (A3.1); the `LOADOUT` column still shows it, so the intel is never
  lost — flagged as an OPEN QUESTION for override.
- **Fixture blindness (medium).** No current fixture has a weapon it cannot
  afford, which is why this slipped through the parent epic; the new matrix adds
  one deliberately.

## Existing state

- `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) resolves a
  `matchup` for **every** `weapon`-kind row, regardless of the economy verdict,
  via `resolveBossMatchup(entry.weaponId, target)`, and appends the marker with
  `withMatchupMarker(...)`.
- The renderer's `rowColour(actionable, matchup)` returns
  `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` / `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR` **before** consulting
  `actionable`, and `rowBackground(matchup)` tints the row — so an
  `unaffordable` (`NEED 40 min`), `gated` (`RING 2`), `upgrade-unaffordable` or
  `capped` (`MAX`) weapon row renders in the bright highlight colour with its
  tint even though nothing can be bought on it.
- `HangarUnlockRow.state` already carries the economy verdict (`owned`, `gated`,
  `unaffordable`, `buyable`, `upgradable`, `upgrade-unaffordable`, `capped`);
  the information needed is present, it is simply not consulted by the highlight.
- `HangarWeaponOption` rows are built from `unlockedWeapons` only (owned, always
  actionable), so the `LOADOUT` column is already always highlighted — and per
  A3 keeps that.
- `GymHangar` renders the same model with **no handlers**, so every rendered row
  reports `actionable: false` while showing the game's colours; the highlight
  must therefore be model data (`src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` pins parity).
- Tests today: `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` ("marks every weapon row …",
  "renders the intel section, the glyph tags and the matchup colours") and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` ("renders the known target intel and ▲/▼
  matchup marks read-only") assert the marker/colour on rows from a 0-salvage
  fixture whose weapons are all **owned** (upgrade rows).

## Desired change

- **Publish the highlight decision in the model.** Beside `matchup`, expose
  whether that verdict should be *highlighted* for this row — true when the row's
  own action is available (`buyable` purchase, `upgradable` upgrade, and every
  `LOADOUT` weapon option), false for `unaffordable`, `gated`,
  `upgrade-unaffordable` and `capped` unlock rows — derived from the economy
  verdicts already on the row (no new economy rule).
- **Render from that flag.** `rowColour` / `rowBackground` consult the highlight
  flag (never the render-time `actionable` flag), so a non-highlighted row falls
  back to the existing row styling while highlighted rows keep today's colour
  and tint. The `▲`/`▼` marker keeps being appended unconditionally by
  `withMatchupMarker`.
- **Cover the matrix with tests** in `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` (model +
  render, with a salvage-bearing fixture for the positive cases) and the gym
  parity case in `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`.
- **Update the docs** that promise the current unconditional marking
  (`README.md` hangar/hex-map paragraphs, GDD §8.2, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`,
  `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *Known-ahead intel*).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — the per-row highlight flag in
  `buildHangarUnlockRows` / `buildHangarWeaponOptions`, and the colour/tint
  decision in `rowColour` / `rowBackground`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` — model + render tests for the `buyable` /
  `unaffordable` / `gated` / `upgradable` / `upgrade-unaffordable` / `capped` /
  `LOADOUT` matrix, and the re-baselined colour assertion.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — parity: the gym renders the same
  suppressed highlight for a non-actionable row.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — record the highlight rule for `GymHangar`.
- `README.md` — the hangar and hex-map paragraphs that describe the marks.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2 config-screen intel paragraph.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — § *Known-ahead intel* (the config screen
  marks "each weapon row").

## Related work

- **AH-0MWMRWCY2001HWGR — When starting a Hex War battle show the ship config
  screen** (completed): the parent epic that introduced the target-aware config
  screen and the unconditional marks this item narrows (children
  AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y pure resolver, AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN model/render,
  AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 gym parity + docs).
- **AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y — Weapon-vs-boss matchup resolver** (completed): the
  pure `resolveBossMatchup` verdict this item presents differently — unchanged.
- **AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat**
  (open): owns the mechanical matchup; this item stays display-only.
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY — Post-MVP Hangar War: hull upgrade bays as a reward
  axis** (open): future economy surface; unaffected but must not inherit a
  misleading highlight.
- Automated find-related report also surfaced `README.md`, `docs/Game Design
  Document.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` as keyword matches
  (documentation touch points).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Asked in-session of the producer; the item was flagged `needsProducerReview`
while the questions were open and is released on their answers.

- **Q1 — Should a non-highlighted weapon row also lose the ▲/▼ text marker, or
  only the colour/tint?**
  Options: (a) keep the marker, suppress colour + tint; (b) hide marker and
  colour together; (c) keep the marker in the muted colour with a `· LOCKED`
  suffix.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the item asks for colour to follow affordability, and
  keeping the tag preserves the CVD-safe intel the parent epic required.
  **Answer (producer): (a)** — keep the marker, suppress only the colour and the
  backing tint. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session. Now recorded as
  AC4 and assumption A2.
- **Q2 — Does "not able to buy" include ring-gated rows (`RING 2`), or only rows
  short of salvage (`NEED … min`)?**
  Options: (a) both; (b) only `unaffordable`.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a gated row is equally unbuyable now, and `canBuy`
  already reports it as `gated` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:528`).
  **Answer (producer): (a)** — both, any row the player cannot buy now. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session. Now recorded as AC1 and assumption A1.
- **Q3 — Do owned weapons keep their highlight when their *upgrade* is
  unaffordable or capped?**
  Options: (a) yes — ownership makes the weapon usable now; (b) no — mute the
  row.
  **Recommended:** (a) (ownership makes the weapon usable now).
  **Answer (producer): split — "if you mean in the equipped/unequipped column
  yes, if you mean in the main selection for upgrade, no."** So the `LOADOUT`
  equipped/unequipped column keeps the highlight for owned weapons, while the
  main purchase/upgrade tree highlights only rows whose own action is available
  (`buyable` / `upgradable`). Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session.
  This **supersedes** the earlier recommended (a) and is recorded as AC3/AC2 and
  assumption A3. Research: the 0-salvage fixtures make those tree rows
  `upgrade-unaffordable`, so their rendered-colour assertions must be
  re-baselined (assumption A6).
- **Q3.1 — Does a `capped` (`MAX`) row count as "no available action"?**
  **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION (producer) — drafted as "yes, not highlighted"
  (A3.1), because the row has nothing left to buy while the `LOADOUT` column
  still shows the weapon's matchup highlighted. Overriding this only changes one
  state in the highlight predicate.

# Close the one-level mineral income gap that collection cannot recover

## Problem statement

The collection re-tune (parent AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J) can raise **collected ÷ spawned** salvage toward its ceiling but **cannot reach the pre-pass-through target of 9.0 (ring 1) / 6.0 (ring 2) minerals/deployment** — a read-only spike on `63f82a791` measured the perfect-collection ceiling at only **7.67 / 5.53**. That item's AC1 explicitly left open the possibility that "the fix may be **harness fidelity**, not a game balance change — investigate before touching drop rates".

**The investigation is now done, and it confirms the harness-fidelity hypothesis.** The headless arena the income measurement is derived from does **not model the game's mineral economy at all**:

- **The arena** seeds a **static mineral field** of `spawns.minerals × 3 = 18` points (`DEFAULT_ARENA_SPAWNS.minerals = 6`), tops the field back up to 6 every 150 ticks from that same 18-point reservoir, and **never drops a mineral on a kill** (it drops power-ups via the real per-kill rule in campaign mode, but not minerals). So the arena's total per-sortie mineral supply is a hard-coded **18**, unrelated to enemy count or player performance.
- **The shipped game** seeds **no mineral field at all** (`PlayScene.resetRunState` clears `this.minerals = []`; the only procedural mineral spawner, `spawnMineralAt`, has *zero* non-test callers). The game's minerals come **entirely from enemy kill drops** through the shared `resolveMineralKillPayout` rule — `2 × round(collected + bonus[0.25–1.25])` per non-asteroid kill, plus 2 per small asteroid (GDD §4.4.1). That is **≈1.5 minerals per non-asteroid kill**, so a level-1 five-wave sortie (42 enemies) supplies **≈63 minerals from kills** — roughly **3.5×** what the arena offers, before enemy mineral absorption inflates the re-drop count further.

So the arena's "perfect collection" ceiling of 7.67 / 5.53 is an **artefact of the harness's 18-mineral field**, not a property of the shipped game's economy. The gap the collection item could not recover is very likely a **measurement-fidelity gap**, not a real balance shortfall.

## Desired outcome

Close the residual gap between the measured perfect-collection ceiling (7.67 / 5.53) and the pre-pass-through baseline (9.0 / 6.0) by **restoring the arena's mineral fidelity to the shipped game, then re-measuring** — before any game balance change is considered:

1. **Confirm and quantify the divergence** between the arena's mineral supply and the shipped game's per-sortie mineral availability (the arena's static 18-field vs the game's kill-drop economy), recording both the mechanism and the measured per-sortie figures.
2. **Fix the fidelity gap** in the arena's mineral supply so the measured per-deployment income reflects the game the unlock tree was balanced against — **producer-ruled path (a): model the game's real mineral kill-drop/absorption economy in the arena** (consume the shared `resolveMineralKillPayout`/`mineralRedropCount` rule rather than a fixed 18-point field), then re-measure ring-1/ring-2 income. A calibration-only shortcut (path b) is not the chosen approach.
3. **If the gap still does not close** after the fidelity fix, decide between an economy-side change to the **game** (spawn/drop rate or capture rate) and recording the achievable ceiling as the accepted balance point — with the measurement as the evidence either way.

## Users

- **Hangar War players** — per-deployment mineral income is the pace at which the unlock tree (hulls, weapons, modifiers) is bought between sorties; a lower income is felt directly as a longer grind.
- **The designer/producer** — owns the trade between the measurement harness's fidelity and the design targets built on it. A harness that under-supplies minerals invalidates every income-derived balance conclusion.

Example user story: *As a Hangar War player, I want my between-sortie income to reflect the field the unlock tree was actually balanced against — so a sortie that looks mineral-rich pays like one, rather than being capped by a harness constant.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- The **arena's per-sortie mineral availability is measured against the shipped game** — the mechanism (static 18-field with no kill-drops vs the game's kill-drop-only economy) and the per-sortie figure at each ring's aggression-selected level are both recorded with the command that reproduces them.
- **The arena's mineral supply is made faithful to the shipped game** so a measured run's mineral supply tracks the game's real kill-drop/absorption economy rather than a fixed 18-point field — **per the producer ruling (a), by modelling the game's kill-drop rule** (consuming the shared `resolveMineralKillPayout`/`mineralRedropCount` behaviour), with the approach recorded.
- **Re-measured income** (seeds 1–3, competent bot, shipped five-wave sortie) is recorded for both rings, and either **moves ring-1/ring-2 minerals/deployment toward 9.0 / 6.0** or records the achievable ceiling as the accepted balance point with the reason.
- Any further economy-side change (game spawn/drop rate or capture rate) is only considered **after** the fidelity fix and is backed by its own measurement; collection routing is **not** changed here (owned by AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J).
- The committed income artifact `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json`, the income guard in `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, and GDD §8.2 *Measured per-deployment income (one-level sortie)* are re-pinned to the resulting measurement, with the reason for each changed pin recorded in a comment.
- A deterministic guard fails if the committed income artifact diverges from a fresh measurement of the shipped bot (or the arena's mineral model diverges from its documented game-faithful contract).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (if it quotes these figures) and the GDD.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player's between-sortie income reflects a field that actually pays the minerals the unlock tree was balanced against, rather than a sortie that cannot spawn enough salvage for collection to matter.

## Constraints

- **No change to collection routing** — that is owned by AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J. This item is the arena/economy side only.
- **Balance figures are measured, not guessed** — use the ring-timing harness; the artifact is the evidence.
- **Arena changes are shared infrastructure** — the headless arena feeds aim, churn, ring-timing and income measurements. Any mineral-model change re-baselines those derived figures and must be re-pinned deliberately, not silently.
- **Determinism preserved** — arena changes must keep same-policy + same-config + same-seed ⇒ byte-identical records (no wall-clock reads, every draw from a seeded stream).
- Prefer modelling the **real game rule** over inventing a new harness constant; a game balance change to compensate for a harness artefact would bake the artefact in.

## Existing state

- **The arena's mineral model** (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`): `mineralReservoir` of `spawns.minerals × 3` (= 18) points at line 963–964; `nextMineral` only decrements (line 1632–1641), so the reservoir is a **hard per-run cap**; replenish tops the field back to 6 every `COLLECTABLE_RESPAWN_TICKS` (150) from the same reservoir (line 2418–2422). In campaign/per-level mode `realSupplyMode` swaps the **power-up** supply to the real per-kill rule but leaves minerals on the static field (line 1877–1891 pushes only `world.drops`, never `world.minerals`).
- **The shipped game's mineral model** (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`): `resetRunState` sets `this.minerals = []` (line 1734) — no seeded field; the only non-test mineral source is `resolveMineralKillPayout` on kill (line 5254–5258), the shared rule in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`; `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount` (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:682`) is `MINERAL_DROP_MULTIPLIER (2) × round(collected + bonus[0.25–1.25])`. `spawnMineralAt` (line 6309) has no production callers.
- **Measured baseline** (parent's spike on `63f82a791`): perfect-collection ceiling **7.67 (ring 1) / 5.53 (ring 2)** minerals/deployment; captured sorties bank **16.75 / 8.0** at the mini-boss checkpoint; capture rates **50 % / 50 %**.
- **The committed income artifact** `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` records 7.44 / 2.67 at 44.4 % / 33.3 % (stale by many commits); the ring-timing guard pins `mineralsPerCapturedDeployment ≈ 16.75` and the ring-1/ring-2 unlock pace.

## Desired change

Make the arena's mineral supply model the shipped game's mineral economy (kill-drops from the shared rule, with the real absorption/re-drop behaviour) — or, if a full model is too broad for this item, calibrate the arena's mineral supply to the measured game-equivalent per-sortie availability — then re-measure ring-1/ring-2 income, re-pin the artifact/guards/GDD, and record whether the 9.0 / 6.0 target is reached or the achievable ceiling is the accepted balance point.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the mineral reservoir, replenish cadence and the kill seam (`destroyHostile`) where a faithful mineral kill-drop/absorption model would live.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — `DEFAULT_ARENA_SPAWNS` / `ArenaSpawns` if the mineral supply becomes configurable or is re-documented.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — the shared game kill-drop rule the arena should consume (single source of truth).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `mineralRedropCount` / `collectMineral` (the absorption → re-drop behaviour to mirror).
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — regenerate from the re-measured income.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — re-pin the income and unlock-pace guards; add a fidelity guard if appropriate.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2 *Measured per-deployment income (one-level sortie)* table, verdict and pace figures.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` / `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — the arena's documented fidelity boundaries (they currently state the seeded mineral harvest stays live).
- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs` — the regeneration CLI (`--one-level --income-out`).

## Related work

- **AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J** — Review the per-deployment mineral income after pass-through collection (parent; its AC1 designated the harness-fidelity path investigated here).
- **AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P** — Implement route-through collection re-tune (sibling; collection routing, out of scope here).
- **AH-0MWLLPAQL003IEXE** — Regenerate income artifact, re-pin guards and update docs (sibling; execution of the re-pin).
- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** — Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment (produced the income artifact + guards).
- **AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB** — the shared mineral kill-drop rule (parent of `mineralKillDrops.ts`).
- **AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT** — Mineral collectable entity and constants.
- **AH-0MUCST1AX00483RX** — Test: Mineral entity lifecycle and collection semantics.
- **AH-0MUX96GJF006CAZP** — Enable mineral collection between waves.
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — the measurement artifact.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — the documented income verdict and pace table.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the arena's documented fidelity boundaries.
- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs` — the regeneration CLI.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — re-baselining the shared arena.** The arena feeds aim, churn, ring-timing and income measurements; changing its mineral model re-baselines all of them. Mitigation: keep the change behind the campaign/one-level supply path where possible, re-pin each affected guard deliberately with a reason, and record the before/after measurement.
- **Risk — modelling absorption is broad.** Mirroring the game's absorb→re-drop behaviour needs enemies to collect minerals in the arena, which the current stationary-hostile model does not do. Mitigation (per ruling (a)): model the real kill-drop rule as the foundation, then add enemy mineral absorption so the re-drop count mirrors `mineralRedropCount`; document any remaining approximation under the arena's existing *fidelity boundary* convention. If absorption proves out of scope, escalate back to the producer rather than silently falling back to a calibration.
- **Risk — the gap may not fully close.** Even with faithful availability the bot may collect less than the game ceiling; the item's ACs allow recording the achievable ceiling as the accepted balance point, so the target is never silently restated.
- **Assumption — the pre-pass-through 9.0 / 6.0 figures are the target** because they are what the GDD and unlock-pace table were baselined on; if the fidelity fix shows they were themselves measured on the unfaithful arena, the re-measured game-faithful figures become the new reference and the unlock pace is re-derived from them.
- **Assumption — small evidence set.** Seeds 1–3 can make a capture-rate move of a deployment or two read as variance; a capture-rate conclusion should be confirmed on a wider seed set.
- **Scope-creep risk:** changing hangar prices, drop rates or the unlock tree is a separate balance item with its own measurement, not something to absorb here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q — Harness fidelity vs game balance (producer-ruled 2026-11-22).** The investigation shows the arena under-supplies minerals (static 18-field, no kill-drops) relative to the shipped game (~63 from kills on a level-1 sortie), so the "perfect-collection ceiling" may be a harness artefact. Should the fix be (a) make the arena model the game's real mineral kill-drop/absorption economy and re-measure, (b) calibrate the arena's mineral supply to the measured game-equivalent availability (smaller change), or (c) record the current arena ceiling as the accepted balance point? **Answer (producer): (a) — model the game's real mineral kill-drop/absorption economy in the arena and re-measure.** Source: interactive reply ("A"). The agent's recommended option was also (a) (falling back to (b) only if a full model proved infeasible).
  - **Evidence (research).** `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`: `mineralReservoir` = `spawns.minerals × 3 = 18` (963–964), `nextMineral` only decrements (1632–1641), replenish from the same reservoir every 150 ticks (2418–2422), and `realSupplyMode` drops only power-ups on kill (1877–1891). `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`: `this.minerals = []` on reset (1734), minerals only from `resolveMineralKillPayout` on kill (5254–5258), `spawnMineralAt` has no production callers. `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:682`: `mineralRedropCount = 2 × round(collected + bonus[0.25–1.25])` ⇒ ≈1.5 minerals per non-asteroid kill. Level-1 five-wave sortie = 42 enemies ⇒ ≈63 minerals from kills.
- **Q — Where does the 9.0 / 6.0 target come from?** — It is the pre-pass-through one-level income measurement the GDD and unlock-pace table were baselined on (parent AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J). **Assumption recorded:** if the fidelity fix re-measures new game-faithful figures, those become the reference and the unlock pace is re-derived from them (the parent AC's documented fallback). # Improve language on win/defeat screen

## Problem statement

The sortie results dialog (the win/defeat screen after a hex deployment) uses ALL CAPS labels and, on defeat, explicitly lists what the player did *not* claim or lost. The claim wording ("GRANT CLAIMED", "GRANT NOT CLAIMED", "SALVAGE FORFEITED") is confusing and unnecessarily negative.

## Users

- Players viewing sortie outcomes after a hex deployment.

Example user story: *As a player who just finished a sortie, I want a clear, friendly results screen so I understand what I earned or lost without decoding shouty labels.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Victory — grant wording:** the `grant` row reads `Technology recovered: <grant entry id>` instead of `GRANT CLAIMED: <grant entry id>`.
2. **Defeat — no unclaimed/lost mention:** the `grant-missed` ("GRANT NOT CLAIMED") and `forfeited` ("SALVAGE FORFEITED") rows are not emitted at all on defeat (both the unclaimed reward and the forfeited minerals/cores are dropped).
3. **Entire screen in sentence case (no ALL CAPS):** every player-visible string on the results screen uses sentence case — label first letter capitalised, all remaining letters lower case, including units and the outcome row.
   - Title: `Sortie results`
   - Outcome: `Victory · score 1200` / `Defeat · score 42`
   - Victory rows: `Salvage banked: +120 minerals, +1 core`; `Technology recovered: wave_laser`; `Special reward: <hull name>`; `Contract bonus: +60 minerals, +1 core`; `Cache payout: +140 minerals`; `Win bonus banked: +250 minerals`
   - Defeat rows that remain: `Strong against: rapid`; `Weak against: mortar`
   - Confirm row: `▶ Continue`
4. **No other screen changes:** the between-sortie defence report / `LAST SORTIE` map news (its own `WIN BONUS BANKED` line in `defenceReport.ts` / `HexMapScene.ts`) is a *different* surface and is out of scope; only the sortie results dialog changes.
5. **Regression coverage:** `sortieResult.test.ts` asserts the exact new strings and the removed row keys; the dialog copy assertions in `HexCombatResultScene.test.ts` (and any integration tests that render the dialog) are updated.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
7. **All related documentation is updated**, specifically `docs/Game Design Document.md` § "The post-battle results dialog" and `README.md`'s `HexMapScene` paragraph, which currently state the dialog shows the unclaimed grant and forfeited salvage and use `VICTORY`/`DEFEAT` headings.

## Impact

Players see a calmer, clearer results screen that states what they earned in normal sentence case without shouting or dwelling on what they missed.

## Constraints

- Dialog text is produced solely by the pure builder `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts`; `HexCombatResultScene` renders title/rows/confirm verbatim. Because the whole screen is in scope, `SORTIE_RESULT_TITLE`, `HEX_COMBAT_RESULT_DEFAULT_TITLE` and `HEX_COMBAT_RESULT_CONFIRM_COPY` are in scope too.
- The `SortieResultView.outcome` discriminator (`'VICTORY' | 'DEFEAT'`) is data, not rendered text — keep it as-is; only the outcome *row text* becomes sentence case.
- `SortieResultRecord.forfeited` and `HexRingDefinition.grants` remain on their types (other consumers / launch data), but `defeatRows()` stops rendering them.
- No gameplay rule, reward calculation or persistence may change — display text only.
- Gym↔game parity: no gym renders this dialog (it is map-only overlay copy), so nothing in `src/scenes/gym/` is affected; confirm in the change.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** sentence case applies to units too (`minerals`, `core`/`cores`), and to the outcome row and units — confirmed by producer Q2 (entire screen).
- **Assumption:** the `outcome` discriminator stays `'VICTORY' | 'DEFEAT'` (data, not display); only its rendered row text changes.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other surfaces use similar ALL-CAPS copy (`LAST SORTIE` map news, `HEX INCOME BANKED`, `RING WON`). These are *different* screens; treat any de-capitalisation of them as new, linked work — not part of this item.
- **Risk (test churn):** several scene/integration tests pin the old strings; the implementer must update every exact-string assertion, not just `sortieResult.test.ts`.
- **Failure mode:** leaving `grant-missed`/`forfeited` in `SortieResultRowKey` after removing the rows creates dead keys; remove them so the type matches behaviour.

## Existing state

- `sortieResult.ts` `victoryRows()` emits `SALVAGE BANKED:`, `GRANT CLAIMED:`, `SPECIAL REWARD:`, `CONTRACT BONUS:`, `CACHE PAYOUT:`, `WIN BONUS BANKED:`.
- `sortieResult.ts` `defeatRows()` emits `STRONG AGAINST:`, `WEAK AGAINST:`, `GRANT NOT CLAIMED:`, `SALVAGE FORFEITED:`.
- Outcome row: `VICTORY · SCORE 1200` / `DEFEAT · SCORE 42`; title: `SORTIE RESULTS`; confirm row: `▶ CONTINUE`.
- `SortieResultRowKey` includes `'grant-missed'` and `'forfeited'`; both become unused once the rows are dropped (remove them from the union).

## Desired change

- Victory rows: sentence-case labels with lower-case units; `GRANT CLAIMED` → `Technology recovered`.
- Defeat rows: drop `GRANT NOT CLAIMED` and `SALVAGE FORFEITED`; sentence-case the remaining `STRONG AGAINST` / `WEAK AGAINST` rows.
- Title, outcome row and confirm row sentence-cased.
- Update `sortieResult.test.ts`, `HexCombatResultScene.test.ts`, and the GDD/README documentation.

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts` — rewrite `victoryRows()` / `defeatRows()` row text, `SORTIE_RESULT_TITLE`, outcome row; drop `grant-missed`/`forfeited` from `SortieResultRowKey`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.test.ts` — new exact-string and row-key assertions.
- `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.ts` — `HEX_COMBAT_RESULT_DEFAULT_TITLE` and `HEX_COMBAT_RESULT_CONFIRM_COPY` sentence case.
- `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.test.ts` — pinned title/confirm/row copy.
- `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` — `SORTIE RESULTS`, `GRANT CLAIMED`, `GRANT NOT CLAIMED`, `SALVAGE FORFEITED` row assertions (plan review: confirmed pinning the old strings).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` — the map integration tests that render the dialog and pin `SORTIE RESULTS`, `SALVAGE BANKED`, `GRANT CLAIMED`, `GRANT NOT CLAIMED`, `SALVAGE FORFEITED` and the `▶ CONTINUE` row (plan review: added — missing from the original key-file list).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.hexMiniBossVictory.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.hangarWar.test.ts` — check any rendered dialog-row expectations (plan review: these pin the map's `WIN BONUS BANKED` news and `getResultsText()`, which AC4 leaves unchanged; verify only).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — § "The post-battle results dialog" bullets (they state the unclaimed grant and forfeited salvage).
- `README.md` — `HexMapScene` paragraph describing the results dialog.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — Candidate D's dialog description (~lines 1125-1130), which repeats the same claim/forfeit wording (plan review: added so the design-of-record does not describe removed rows).

## Related work

- AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC "We need an outer loop" (completed) — the sortie results dialog was designed as part of the outer loop.
- AH-0MUTYK6WV005ZK6G "Defeat screen treatment VFX" (completed) — the defeat screen visuals this text sits over.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVF2H4UL007IJT4** – [test-failure] PlayScene.test.ts > AC4 — defeating all 4 phases wins the run at the game-over screen — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MUTYK6WV005ZK6G** – Defeat screen treatment VFX (completed)
- **AH-0MWW5JJLV000SK95** – Hangar screen needs more detail about the various options (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: case, claim, claimed, defeat, grant, language, minerals, rather, recovered, rewards, screen, upper, use, win
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — matched: case, claim, claimed, defeat, grant, minerals, rather, recovered, rewards, screen, use, win
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: case, claim, claimed, defeat, grant, minerals, rather, recovered, rewards, screen, use, win

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q5 — Is `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` in scope?**
  - Answer (agent, repo research during plan review): yes — it renders the dialog through `HexMapScene` and pins `SORTIE RESULTS`, `SALVAGE BANKED`, `GRANT CLAIMED`, `GRANT NOT CLAIMED`, `SALVAGE FORFEITED` and `▶ CONTINUE`; added to Key Files so AC5 covers it. Source: `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` lines ~1655-1735.
- **Q6 — Is `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` in scope?**
  - Answer (agent, repo research during plan review): yes — Candidate D (~lines 1125-1130) describes the dialog as stating the grant "did not claim" and the salvage that "was forfeited", so it is a related document under AC7. Source: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.


- **Q1 — Casing style.** The description says "Do not use upper case on this screen, use camel case", but the example replacement "Technology recovered" is sentence case. Which style should the labels use?
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-11-25):** sentence case. Source: interactive reply. Final accepted answer overrides the earlier "camel case" wording: first letter capitalised, rest lower case (e.g. `Salvage banked:`, `Technology recovered:`).
- **Q2 — Scope of the casing change.** Does it apply to the whole screen or only the reward/intel row labels?
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-11-25):** entire screen — title, outcome row, units and the confirm button are all in scope. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Defeat removal.** Confirm "both minerals and rewards" means remove the `GRANT NOT CLAIMED` (reward) and `SALVAGE FORFEITED` (minerals/cores) rows on defeat.
  - Answer (agent, reasonable assumption recorded during intake): yes — both rows are removed; boss strengths/weaknesses are *not* "what was not claimed", so they stay. Source: work-item description + `sortieResult.ts` `defeatRows()`.
- **Q4 — Does "this screen" include the between-sortie map news / defence report?**
  - Answer (agent, repo research): no — the `WIN BONUS BANKED` line in `defenceReport.ts` / `HexMapScene.ts` belongs to the map's `LAST SORTIE` news, a different surface; it is unchanged. Source: `docs/Game Design Document.md` § post-battle results dialog + `defenceReport.ts`.

# Bug: Ring-2's modifier grants have no hangar catalogue entry

Discovered-from: AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 (deliberately out of scope there — same class of drift, different fix).

## Problem statement

`hex-r2-8` grants `armour-plating`, `hex-r2-9` grants `systems-upgrade` and `hex-r2-10` grants `firepower-up` (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`). `resolveHexGrant` falls through to its final `kind: 'modifier'` default (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts:320`), so each id lands in `hangar.ownedModifiers` with **no catalogue entry**. Consequences:

- invisible in `buildHangarUnlockRows` (catalogue-driven);
- dropped by `resolveActiveLoadout` → `ownedEntriesOf`, so never equippable;
- **no `ModifierEffect`**, so the grant has no observable effect on any deployment.

Three of ring 2's twelve hexes therefore pay out a reward that cannot be seen, equipped or felt.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** capturing three ring-2 hexes should leave the fleet measurably stronger; today it writes a string into a save field.
  - *"As a player who has just beaten the Bone Sibyl, I want the armour plating I was promised to show up in my hangar and change how my deployments play."*
- **Player (reward legibility):** reward names should describe what they do, so `firepower-up` must not silently resolve to an extra life.
  - *"As a player, I want the reward name on the hex to match the effect I actually get."*
- **Maintainer:** the effect-free allowlist must shrink, not become a permanent dumping ground.
  - *"As a maintainer, I want the grant guard to fail closed on the next uncatalogued grant instead of tolerating a growing exception list."*

## Design decision (recorded — producer chose the recommended hybrid; AC1 satisfied)

The three ids map **exactly** onto `HullUpgrades { armour, firepower, systems }` — the three authored hull-upgrade axes in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`. That suggests the ring data means these as *permanent hull training* rewards rather than generic modifiers. Candidate fixes:

- **(a) Hull-upgrade rewards.** Fold the grant into a hull's permanent upgrade level, feeding `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` / `resolvePlayerStrength`. Most faithful to the vocabulary, but needs a decided home for a *mutable* hull upgrade level.
- **(b) Author three modifier entries** using today's `ModifierEffect` kinds (`extra-lives`, `defence`, `defence-skill`). No model change and cheapest — but `firepower`/`systems` have no matching effect, so the entry names would misdescribe what they do. Only acceptable if the effect model is knowingly renamed to match.
- **(c) Extend `ModifierEffect`** with firepower/systems effects. New model surface, but keeps everything on the modifier path.

### Research findings that constrain the choice

- **No mutable hull-upgrade level exists.** `HullDefinition.upgrades` is authored constant (`readonly HullUpgrades`), and `HangarState` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) has no hull-upgrade field — its only purchased-level rows are `weaponLevels` and `powerUpLevels`. So option (a) as written needs either a **new saved field** (which collides with AC6's "no migration and no schema change") or a **derived** rule that reads ownership of the three ids and adds a bucket level at rating time (no schema change).
- **Today's effect vocabulary cannot express two of the three names.** Only two modifiers are shipped: `hardened_plating` (`extra-lives`) and `anti_maw_plating` (`defence-skill` vs `maw-of-ashes`). Option (b) would therefore ship a `firepower-up` that does not touch firepower.
- **An alias-only fix is already possible and would be wrong-ish.** `GRANT_ALIASES` (`src/core/hangarWar/grantAliases.ts`) re-points authored spellings at catalogue ids (`extra-life` → `hardened_plating`, `waveLaser` → `wave_laser`). Re-pointing all three at the two existing modifiers is the cheapest possible fix, but three distinct ring-2 rewards would then pay the same thing.
- **One rating formula, and it moves balance.** `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` (`baseDefence + 3×armour + 2×firepower + 2×systems`) is the single rating expression; `resolvePlayerStrength` feeds it to `ringAggressionBudget`, so any rating bump raises the frontier's aggression budget mass (AC4).

### Decision (producer, 2026-11-27: "As recommended")

Ship the **hybrid of (a) and (c)**: the three ids become catalogue modifier entries whose effect is **one** new `ModifierEffect` kind naming a hull stat bucket (`armour` | `firepower` | `systems`) plus a level. The effect is folded through the existing `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` formula — no second rating path — and ownership stays in `hangar.ownedModifiers`, so an existing save that already holds these ids gains the effect on load with no migration and no schema change (AC6 for free), the hangar gains a named row (AC2), and the effect is measurable as a rating delta (AC3).

Mechanically, this means: `armour-plating` → `{ kind: 'hull-upgrade', bucket: 'armour', level: 1 }`, `systems-upgrade` → `{ bucket: 'systems', level: 1 }`, `firepower-up` → `{ bucket: 'firepower', level: 1 }`, each authored as a grant-only modifier entry (zero price, `GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING`), exactly as the derived weapon entries are grant-only today.

**Why the hybrid over (a) alone:** (a) needs a mutable hull-upgrade level, and no such field exists — `HullDefinition.upgrades` is authored constant and `HangarState` carries only `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels`, so (a) alone would add a saved field and a migration of its own, contradicting AC6.

**Why not (b):** today's effect kinds (`extra-lives`, `defence`, `defence-skill`) cannot express two of the three names; option (b) ships a `firepower-up` that does not touch firepower.

**Why not (c) alone:** two bespoke effects (`firepower`, `systems`) duplicate the bucket vocabulary that `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` / `HullUpgrades` already own; one bucketed kind keeps a single expression and lets `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` stay the only arithmetic.

**Why not an alias re-point:** `GRANT_ALIASES` could map all three onto the two shipped modifiers, but three distinct ring-2 rewards would then pay the same thing.

**Permanence (part of the decision):** hull training is permanent and **un-equipped** — the effect is read from ownership (`ownedModifiers`), never from `activeLoadout.modifiers`. This is what makes AC6 free: the ids are already in `ownedModifiers` in existing saves, so no auto-equip write and therefore no migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — The chosen option is recorded on this item with its reasoning and the rejected alternatives, before any code is written. **Satisfied:** the hybrid was chosen by the producer on 2026-11-27 (see *Design decision* above and Appendix Q1); implementation may proceed against it.
- **AC2** — Each of `armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade` and `firepower-up` has a modelled outcome that is visible in the hangar once owned (a named row) and survives `resolveActiveLoadout` / the defender path as applicable.
- **AC3** — The effect is **measurable**, not just ownership: capture the granting hex and assert a specific before/after change (starting lives, defence rating, or firepower) through the shipped pure rules — not merely that the id appears in an owned set.
- **AC4** — The change stays inside the ring-2 aggression-band budget (`ringAggressionBudget` / `DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING`) and does not trivialise ring 2; demonstrated with the existing budget tests rather than asserted.
- **AC5** — The three ids are removed from `HEX_GRANT_EFFECT_FREE_ALLOWLIST` (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) introduced as AC5(e) of AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91, so the guard tightens rather than permanently excusing them. The three suites that pin the allowlist contents are updated in the same change: `src/core/hangarWar/hexGrantAcceptance.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts` and `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts`.
- **AC6** — Existing saves already holding these ids gain the effect on load with no migration and no schema change; a save that holds none is unchanged.
- **AC7** — Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md): the change is pure rules + data, so no new `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` divergence row — or one is recorded with its reason.
- **AC8** — Documentation reflects the decision: `docs/EVALUATION.md` no longer lists the three ids as effect-free, the `docs/Game Design Document.md` sentence that calls them "strength entries" is updated to name the modelled effect, and any changed modelled loadout in `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` / `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` is regenerated deliberately rather than incidentally.
- **AC9** — Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

Ring 2's three upgrade hexes start paying out something the player can see and feel, instead of writing a string into a save field that changes nothing.

## Constraints

- No second copy of an effect rule: reuse `ModifierEffect` / `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` rather than adding a parallel rating path; the bucket vocabulary is `HullUpgrades` / `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS`, never a fresh list of stat names.
- The grant is permanent hull training: read it from ownership (`ownedModifiers`), not from `activeLoadout.modifiers`, so an existing save needs no auto-equip write (AC6).
- The three entries are grant-only (zero price, `GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING`), like the derived grant-only weapon entries — no purchase path.
- Do not silently drop the grants from the ring data — three hexes would then pay nothing at all.
- Pure rules + authored data only: no Phaser, scene or DOM imports in the changed logic; scenes only present and persist.
- Do not edit the ring data's authored spelling (`armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade`, `firepower-up`) to dodge the guard — the guard must be satisfied by modelling, not renaming.

## Existing state

- `resolveHexGrant` (`captureCycle.ts`) resolves alias → catalogue entry → shipped weapon → `hull-*` prefix → **`kind: 'modifier'` fallback**; the fallback is the path these three ids take.
- `HEX_GRANT_EFFECT_FREE_ALLOWLIST` is the only reader-side exception to guard (e) in `validateHangarCatalogue`; its comment already names this item as the owner of the fix.
- The hangar's owned-modifier reads are `buildHangarUnlockRows` (catalogue-driven, so no row today), `resolveActiveLoadout` → `ownedEntriesOf` (filters on catalogue membership, so the ids are dropped), and `resolvePlayerStrength` (adds only `effect.kind === 'defence'` modifiers).
- `ModifierEffect` today: `extra-lives`, `defence`, `defence-skill`.
- The defender/bot side already has a mutable per-bot upgrade vocabulary (`DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`, `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS`, `botUpgrade.ts`'s `train` verdict) — useful precedent for how a stored, mutable upgrade level is expressed without a second formula, but it is *bot* state, not fleet state.

## Desired change

- Give each of the three ids a catalogue-modelled outcome, one effect expression and one rating formula (AC2/AC3, no duplicate rule).
- Shrink the effect-free allowlist to empty (or to a documented non-modifier reason) and keep guard (e) failing closed (AC5).
- Prove the balance and save-compatibility properties with the existing budget/snapshot tests rather than prose (AC4/AC6).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — `hex-r2-8/9/10` grants (authored data, unchanged spelling)
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts:320` — the `kind: 'modifier'` fallback and grant resolution
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — `ModifierEffect`, `HullUpgrades`, `HEX_GRANT_EFFECT_FREE_ALLOWLIST`, `validateHangarCatalogue` guard (e)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `resolvePlayerStrength`, `defenderRatingFromUpgrades`, `ownedEntriesOf`, `buildHangarUnlockRows`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `ringAggressionBudget` (AC4 witness)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexGrantAcceptance.test.ts`, `captureCycle.test.ts`, `hangarCatalogue.test.ts`, `hangarEconomy.test.ts` — the allowlist/effect/budget witnesses
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` + `hangarWarStore.test.ts` — the save round-trip that witnesses AC6 (an old payload holding the ids gains the effect on load, unchanged on write)
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` — the `buildHangarUnlockRows` witness for AC2 (a named, owned row appears; no scene-code change expected)
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` + `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` — the timing model already names these grants and must stay consistent
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — currently documents the three ids as effect-free
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (~line 3557) — currently calls the three ids "strength entries" in the ring-2 grant list (AC8)

## Plan (plan_complete)

**Sizing decision — one slice, no child decomposition.** The item is a single
bug with a decided design (AC1), Small effort and Medium risk, so the plan
skill's step-1 heuristic applies: measurable ACs plus an implementation sketch
in the description means it is directly implementable. Splitting it would also
be actively harmful: AC5 requires the allowlist removal **and** the three pinned
suites to land in one change, and AC6's witness is a save round-trip of the same
change, so any child split would create partial states the guard (e) and the
save round-trip cannot express. Implementation order below is the plan; the
item stays one worktree/session.

### Implementation order (red-first)

1. **Red — effect vocabulary and resolution.** Extend `ModifierEffect` with

# Arc planner cannot compensate a fade whose total overlap is not a whole sample step

`--fade-duration` accepts any non-negative millisecond value, but the arc planner can only compensate fade overlap in whole 0.1 s sample steps (10 Hz series), so a fade whose **total** overlap is not a multiple of that step leaves a sub-step residual that trips a hard shortfall.

## Problem statement

`compensateFadeOverlap` (`scripts/intensity-arc.mjs`) grows windows in whole samples via `growWindowBy`'s `floor(remaining / stepSeconds)`, so a required compensation that is not an exact multiple of `1 / sampleRateHz` can never be absorbed: the loop stops with a sub-step residual, and `planIntensityArc` throws `IntensityArcShortfallError` blaming the footage ("the selected windows leave only 35.300s of footage") even when there is plenty of slack. Any fade where `(windows − 1) × fadeSeconds` is off the 10 Hz grid fails this way — e.g. 4 windows × 450 ms needs 1.35 s, of which 1.3 s is absorbed and 0.05 s is not.

## Users

Producers cutting the promo with `npm run capture:promo` / `node scripts/render-promo.mjs`.

- As a producer, I want `--fade-duration 450` to produce a promo instead of failing with a message about footage I know I have, so that I can pick a fade length that suits the material.
- As a producer, when a run genuinely cannot deliver the arc, I want the error to name the real cause (the sample-step-quantised compensation) so that I do not go re-capture footage I already have.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A plan whose total fade overlap is off the sample grid completes: a 4-window plan with `fadeSeconds: 0.45` (total 1.35 s) is planned without throwing, and its compensation is rounded **up** to the whole sample grid (1.4 s) — the rendered arc is the 34 s target plus at most one sample step (34.05 s here), never a shorter arc.
- An on-grid total is unchanged: a plan whose `(windows − 1) × fadeSeconds` is already a whole number of sample steps (the default 300 ms, or 500 ms) still renders exactly the arc target, with no extra footage added — the existing "rendered timeline totals 34 s" guarantees hold unchanged.
- The residual shortfall path is honest: when the footage genuinely cannot absorb the rounded-up compensation, the thrown message names the rounded compensation and the sample step (10 Hz / 0.1 s) rather than implying that the footage itself is short.
- A regression test covers the reported reproduction (4 windows, `--fade-duration 450`) and asserts the chosen behaviour, including that the planner's `planTotals` numbers are internally consistent (footage − fade = rendered).
- `--help` (`USAGE_TEXT`, `scripts/render-promo.mjs`) documents the sample-step constraint: the fade compensation is rounded up to the 10 Hz sample grid, so the rendered arc may exceed the 34 s target by less than one sample step; the forwarded `--fade-duration` value itself is unchanged.
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5.1 step 3 describes the same rounding behaviour.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer who passes a fade duration off the 10 Hz sample grid gets a rendered promo instead of a confusing "not enough footage" failure on footage that was never short, and the error that does remain names the real cause.

## Constraints

- Planner primitives stay pure (no clock, no randomness) and the plan stays byte-for-byte reproducible from the same inputs; determinism tests must keep passing.
- The value forwarded to `vidc` is unchanged: the producer's `--fade-duration` is still passed verbatim so the renderer cross-fades exactly what was asked for; only the planner's compensation is quantised. `buildVidcArgv`'s argv contract tests must keep passing.
- The default 300 ms fade is already on the grid, so default runs (and the real-vidc e2e expectations) must be bit-identical to today.
- No new CLI flag, no new config field, no change to band selection, window nudge or shortfall semantics for genuinely unavailable bands.
- Round **up** (never down): the module's stated posture is "never a quietly shorter arc", so a residual must be absorbed by extra footage, not by delivering less than the target.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 10 Hz grid (`DEFAULT_INTENSITY_ARC_CONFIG.sampleRateHz`) is the only constraint; a retuned `sampleRateHz` quantises to its own step, so the fix must derive the step from the config rather than hard-coding 0.1 s.
- **Risk:** rounding up can still fail when a run's slack is smaller than one sample step — mitigated by making the message name the rounded demand (AC 3) so it is not mistaken for a footage shortage.
- **Risk:** `planTotals.renderedSeconds` legitimately leaves the exact 34 s for off-grid fades; downstream assertions and the `.otio` metadata must tolerate `34 s + residual ≤ 34 s + one step` rather than pinning 34 s for every fade.
- **Scope-creep risk:** retuning the fade grid itself, changing `vidc`'s fade handling, or re-specifying band selection are out of scope — record them as linked work items instead.

## Existing state

- `compensateFadeOverlap` (L1079) computes `extraSeconds = (windows − 1) × fadeSeconds`, then distributes it in `stepSeconds` increments through `growWindowBy` (L1028), whose `Math.floor(remaining / stepSeconds)` silently drops a sub-step remainder. It returns that remainder.
- `planIntensityArc` (L1215) treats any non-zero remainder as a shortfall and throws `IntensityArcShortfallError` with a footage-blaming message.
- `planTotals` reports `fadeSeconds = (windows − 1) × config.fadeSeconds` and `renderedSeconds = footageSeconds − fadeSeconds` — with rounded-up compensation the rendered total is therefore `34 s + residual` and both numbers stay truthful.
- `scripts/intensity-arc.test.ts` L834 pins "compensates the fade overlap so the rendered timeline totals 34 s" for the default fade; `scripts/render-promo.e2e.test.ts` L239 pins `totals.fadeSeconds` for the default; `scripts/render-promo.test.ts` L237 pins the verbatim `--fade-duration 450` argv and L299 pins `renderedSeconds ≈ 34` for an on-grid 500 ms fade.

## Desired change

Quantise the *demand* rather than the loop: in `compensateFadeOverlap`, compute the compensation as the smallest whole number of sample steps that covers `(windows − 1) × fadeSeconds` (i.e. `ceil(total / step) × step`), then distribute it through the existing even-growth loop. Distinguishing a sub-step residual from a real footage shortage in the `planIntensityArc` message keeps the diagnosis honest. Document the rounding in `USAGE_TEXT` and in the planner docs, and cover the reported reproduction with a regression test.

## Key Files

- `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` — `compensateFadeOverlap` (L1079) demand rounding; `growWindowBy` (L1028) and the shortfall message in `planIntensityArc` (L1215) need the rounded demand named.
- `scripts/intensity-arc.test.ts` — new regression beside the existing fade-compensation spec (L834): 4 windows × `fadeSeconds: 0.45` plans and renders within one sample step of the target; an on-grid total adds no extra footage.
- `scripts/render-promo.mjs` — `USAGE_TEXT` (L110) `--fade-duration` entry documents the sample-step quantisation.
- `scripts/render-promo.test.ts` — help-text/doc contract assertion for the new sentence.
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — §7.5.1 step 3 records the rounded-up compensation and the ≤ one sample step overshoot.

## Related work

- **discovered-from: AH-0MWM295HP001X1ZU** — found while writing the vidc e2e suite (parent AH-0MWLYWYGK004JR2A).
- **AH-0MWPD4SGJ005LAPR** — Planner window selection and fade compensation: defines the `rendered = Σ durations − (clips − 1) × fadeSeconds` contract this item refines; its AC (d) ("rendered-timeline total of 34 s") is what the round-up rule relaxes by at most one sample step.
- **AH-0MWPD4OZH001M74F** — Arc planner test corpus and fixture builders: supplies `syntheticCorpus` / `FULL_ARC_PLATEAUS`, the harness a regression test will reuse.
- **AH-0MWPD4QRO007WMJ1** — Intensity-arc planner ingest and band config: owns `sampleRateHz: 10` and `fadeSeconds: 0.3` in `DEFAULT_INTENSITY_ARC_CONFIG`.
- **AH-0MWM293GY004WC5J** — Docs: cross-fade behaviour; `AH-0MWM291MV005P336` — Duration accounting in plan, report and help (the other pipeline's fade arithmetic, deliberately not touched here).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWPD4OZH001M74F** – Arc planner test corpus and fixture builders (completed)
- **AH-0MWPD4SGJ005LAPR** – Planner window selection and fade compensation (completed)
- **AH-0MW3MWRZ5003KVR3** – Replace fixed-duration dive with fixed-speed, distance-proportional dive in Diver.ts (completed — unrelated, keyword match only)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — keyword match only
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — keyword match only
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — keyword match only

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should an off-grid fade total be rejected up front or compensated to the sample grid?" — **Recommended:** quantise the compensation and proceed — the AC permits either, and rejecting values `vidc` accepts would lose capability for a purely internal rounding limit. Answer (agent, research): quantise the *demand* up to the sample grid and proceed. Research: `scripts/intensity-arc.mjs` (L1028/L1079/L1215) shows the residual is a planner artefact, not a footage limit; `scripts/render-promo.mjs`'s `USAGE_TEXT` and `resolveArcConfig` show the fade is forwarded verbatim to `vidc`, so the renderer needs no change. **OPEN QUESTION** only in the sense that the producer may redirect to the reject-up-front branch — the choice is cheap to reverse (one module plus its docs).
- Q: "Round the compensation up or down when a sub-step residual remains?" — **Recommended:** round up — the module's documented posture is "never a quietly shorter arc" (`planIntensityArc` prose), so delivering 33.95 s would be a worse failure than a ≤ 100 ms overshoot. Answer (agent, research): round up; the rendered total is `arc target + residual` and `planTotals` already reports footage and fade separately, so both numbers stay truthful. Research: `planTotals` (L~1250) computes `renderedSeconds = footageSeconds − fadeSeconds`; existing tests pin exactness only for on-grid fades.
- Q: "Should `--fade-duration` itself be quantised (so the forwarded value changes), or only the planner's compensation?" — **Recommended:** only the compensation — quantising the forwarded value would silently render a different fade from the one requested and would break the pinned argv contract. Answer (agent, research): only the compensation. Research: `buildVidcArgv` pushes the raw `options.fadeDuration`, and `scripts/render-promo.test.ts` L237 pins `--fade-duration 450` verbatim.

# Elites should spawn ships close to their position

## Problem statement

A `splitter` elite releases its two ordinary children **after** its hull has
already vanished, at a fixed pre-set offset from the wreck
(`ELITE_SPLITTER_CHILD_OFFSET_PX = 18`) and with no impulse. The children
therefore materialise beside a corpse and stay put (drifting with the
formation), so the player never sees the children "escape" the doomed elite —
the split reads as a static two-body replacement rather than a burst of ships.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the split to read as a dramatic, legible event: the
  children visibly burst out of the dying elite at high speed, scatter clear of
  it, and only then turn to attack.

**User story:** As a player destroying an elite, I want its children to fly out
of the wreck at high speed and get clear of the doomed elite before engaging
me, so the splitter feels alive rather than like two ships blinking in beside a
corpse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `splitter` elite's children appear at — or within a few pixels of — the
  elite's own position and burst outward from the wreck at a high speed
  (materially faster than the archetype's ordinary `driftSpeed`), instead of
  materialising at a pre-set deployment distance.
- The burst happens on the lethal blow **before** the elite's hull is hidden: the
  children are spawned while the elite is still visible, so the player sees
  them shoot out of the doomed elite and the elite then explodes.
- The outward fan is deterministic: the same seed + wave produces the same child
  directions and the split never consumes an RNG draw (the documented spliterator
  determinism invariant is preserved).
- After the burst each child settles into its ordinary archetype movement and is
  fully combat-ready — damageable and able to attack the player exactly like
  today's ordinary split children; the burst is a transient outward impulse, not
  a permanent movement-class change or an immunity window.
- The split decision and the burst speed/geometry live once in the shared core
  (`eliteMechanics`) and are consumed by both `PlayScene` and
  `GymFodderEnemies` through the existing `spawnEliteSplitChild` seam (gym↔game
  parity, per the project AGENTS.md convention) — no divergent per-scene copy.
- Wave accounting is unchanged: children are wave-registered before the parent's
  death is accounted, so a wave can never clear in the gap between the parent's
  destruction and its children's registration.
- Testing/validation: unit tests pin the burst decision and constants in
  `src/scenes/core/eliteMechanics.test.ts`; the end-to-end seam walk in
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.elite.test.ts` and the gym parity test in
  `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.elite.test.ts` assert
  "spawn-at-wreck → burst outward → settle combat-ready"; the repo-wide
  duplicate-body/parity guards (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `gymParityDocs.test.ts`) pass.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player destroying an elite now sees its children blast out of the wreck at
high speed and scatter clear of the doomed hull before turning to attack — the
split reads as a live escape, not two ships blinking in beside a corpse.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **Determinism preserved (documented invariant).** Splits never consume an RNG
  draw; the mirrored left/right fan direction is kept and merely gains an
  outward impulse. Evidence: `eliteMechanics.ts` comment ("a split never
  consumes an RNG draw and the same seeded run reproduces the same fan") and the
  determinism child AH-0MWU665DM00669U0.
- **Ships only.** Children remain ordinary counted enemies of the elite's
  archetype — no new entity class, no invulnerability window, no change to wave
  accounting.
- **Transient burst.** The impulse settles into the archetype's ordinary
  movement after a short travel; children are not given a new permanent
  movement class.
- **Shared core, both consumers.** Per the project Gym↔game parity convention
  (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`), the burst must run the same code in
  `PlayScene` and every gym scene that fields the splitter.
- **Assumption — "just before destroyed" means on the lethal blow while the hull
  is still visible.** Today's seam spawns children in `finaliseEnemyKill`, which
  runs *after* `destroySelf()` has already hidden the hull and started the
  explosion. The requirement is read as: spawn the children from the still-intact
  elite on the lethal blow (before `destroySelf()`), so the burst is visible
  leaving the doomed elite. This is a real ordering change, not just a visual
  tweak; it keeps the wave-accounting ordering property (children registered
  before the parent's death is accounted).
- **Assumption — "high speed" means a dedicated, tunable burst constant** pegged
  to the existing shared speed vocabulary rather than re-using `driftSpeed`.
- **Assumption — children remain fully combat-active during the burst** (they can
  be hit and can hit the player) because the item says they must be "ready to
  attack the player". A settle delay/immunity was not requested and would be
  cheap to add later.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/eliteMechanics.ts` — `ELITE_SPLITTER_CHILD_COUNT = 2`,
  `ELITE_SPLITTER_CHILD_OFFSET_PX = 18`; `eliteSplitChildOffset(index)` returns
  `{x: ±18, y: 0}`; `applyEliteDeathBehaviour` dispatches to the per-scene
  `spawnSplitChild(offset)` seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `finaliseEnemyKill()` calls
  `_applyEliteDeathBehaviour(enemy)` before `onEnemyDestroyed(enemy)`; this runs
  after the entity's `destroySelf()` (hull already hidden, explosion started).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — the default no-op
  `spawnEliteSplitChild(_enemy, _offset)` seam.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`spawnEliteSplitChild`, ~line 2425) — spawns an
  ordinary child via `createEnemyFromConfig` at `enemy.x/y + offset`, registers
  it in `spawned` and `waveManager.registerDynamicSpawn(1)`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` (`spawnEliteSplitChild`, ~line 1179) —
  the same shape through the gym's formation factory + `registerDynamicEntity`.
- Parity/mechanics documentation: `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (Elite (anomaly) parity

  per-entity velocity.** `PlayScene` positions every enemy from its
  `SpawnedEnemy.startX/startY + driftX` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:2370`), and a

  fractional offset (`GymFodderEnemies.spawnEliteSplitChild`, ~line 1179). So
